diagrams.title: AP2 alternative path: verifying mandates and receipts in a dispute
diagrams.description: Sequence diagram: AP2 alternative path: verifying mandates and receipts in a dispute. 3 participants: Merchant, Credential Provider, and Dispute verifier. 7 steps, 2 crossing a trust boundary, 1 failure branch. diagrams.title: AP2 failure: invalid_credential on a broken mandate chain
diagrams.description: Sequence diagram: AP2 failure: invalid_credential on a broken mandate chain. 2 participants: Shopping Agent and Credential Provider. 4 steps, 2 crossing a trust boundary, 1 failure branch. Based on ap2 v0.2 (2026-04-28). Step 1: Shopping Agent to Credential Provider: Present open and closed Payment Mandates. This step crosses a trust boundary. Step 2: Credential Provider to Credential Provider: Verify the chain under Delegate SD-JWT. If The chain verifies but the closed mandate changes a value the open mandate fixed, such as the payee: invalid_mandate: the mandate does not approve this action; terminal. Step 3: Credential Provider to Shopping Agent: Payment Receipt: status Error, invalid_credential. This step crosses a trust boundary. Step 4: Shopping Agent to Shopping Agent: Record the rejection.

diagrams.title: AP2 failure: unresolved_constraint and fallback to human present
diagrams.description: Sequence diagram: AP2 failure: unresolved_constraint and fallback to human present. 4 participants: User, Shopping Agent, Trusted Surface, and Merchant. 7 steps, 5 crossing a trust boundary, 1 failure branch. Based on ap2 v0.2 (2026-04-28). Step 1: Shopping Agent to Merchant: Token plus open and closed Checkout Mandates. This step crosses a trust boundary. Step 2: Merchant to Merchant: Evaluate every constraint. Step 3: Merchant to Shopping Agent: Checkout Receipt: status Error, unresolved_constraint. This step crosses a trust boundary. Step 4: Shopping Agent to Trusted Surface: Fall back: request approval of closed Mandate Content. This step crosses a trust boundary. Step 5: Trusted Surface to User: Show the exact checkout; authenticate. If The user declines: The purchase stops; the open mandate remains bounded by its exp. Step 6: Trusted Surface to Shopping Agent: User-signed closed mandates. This step crosses a trust boundary. Step 7: Shopping Agent to Merchant: Present the user-signed closed Checkout Mandate. This step crosses a trust boundary.

This step crosses a trust boundary. If A constraint type the verifier will not know is included: Every verifier must fail it later with unresolved_constraint. Step 3: Trusted Surface to User: Show the constraints; authenticate and get consent. Step 4: Trusted Surface to Trusted Surface: Sign open mandates with user_sk. Step 5: Trusted Surface to Shopping Agent: Return the open mandates; the user leaves. This step crosses a trust boundary. Step 6: Shopping Agent to Merchant: Build a cart autonomously. This step crosses a trust boundary. Step 7: Merchant to Shopping Agent: Signed checkout (checkout_jwt); mandate required. This step crosses a trust boundary. Step 8: Shopping Agent to Shopping Agent: Select open mandates that fit. Step 9: Shopping Agent to Shopping Agent: Sign closed mandates with agent_sk. Step 10: Shopping Agent to Credential Provider: Present open and closed Payment Mandates. This step crosses a trust boundary. If The amount is outside payment.amount_range or the payee is not allowed: Payment Receipt with status Error. The error the specification gives for a closed mandate that cannot be shown to meet the constraints is unresolved_constraint. If The closed mandate is not signed by the key in cnf, or sd_hash does not match: invalid_credential; terminal. Step 11: Credential Provider to Shopping Agent: Payment token. This step crosses a trust boundary. Step 12: Shopping Agent to Merchant: Token plus open and closed Checkout Mandates. This step crosses a trust boundary. Step 13: Merchant to Merchant Payment Processor: Initiate payment with the token and both hashes. This step crosses a trust boundary. Step 14: Merchant Payment Processor to Shopping Agent: Payment Receipt. This step crosses a trust boundary. Step 15: Merchant to Shopping Agent: Checkout Receipt. This step crosses a trust boundary. Step 16: Shopping Agent to Shopping Agent: Store the tuple and narrow the open mandate.

diagrams.title: AP2 v0.2 human present: the user signs closed mandates on a Trusted Surface
diagrams.description: Sequence diagram: AP2 v0.2 human present: the user signs closed mandates on a Trusted Surface. 7 participants: User, Shopping Agent, Trusted Surface, Merchant, Credential Provider, Network, and Merchant Payment Processor. 16 steps, 12 crossing a trust boundary, 8 failure branches. Based on ap2 v0.2 (2026-04-28). Step 1: User to Shopping Agent: Start shopping. Step 2: Shopping Agent to Merchant: Build a cart over the commerce protocol. This step crosses a trust boundary. If The merchant does not accept mandates for this action: It can answer mandates_not_supported, a signal to fall back to a non-agentic flow. Step 3: Merchant to Shopping Agent: Signed checkout (checkout_jwt); mandate required. This step crosses a trust boundary. If The cart changes after this point: The merchant will reject any mandate whose checkout_hash does not match its latest checkout_jwt. Step 4: Shopping Agent to Credential Provider: Fetch instrument options. This step crosses a trust boundary. Step 5: Shopping Agent to Trusted Surface: Request approval of Checkout and Payment Mandate Content. This step crosses a trust boundary. Step 6: Trusted Surface to User: Show the content; authenticate and get consent. If The user declines: No mandate is signed and nothing is presented. Step 7: Trusted Surface to Trusted Surface: Sign closed mandates with user_sk. Step 8: Trusted Surface to Shopping Agent: Return the signed mandates. This step crosses a trust boundary. Step 9: Shopping Agent to Credential Provider: Present the closed Payment Mandate. This step crosses a trust boundary. If The signature or chain does not verify: Payment Receipt with status Error and error invalid_credential; terminal. If The mandate does not approve this payment: Payment Receipt with error invalid_mandate; terminal. Step 10: Credential Provider to Network: Share the mandate, get a scoped credential (optional). This step crosses a trust boundary. Step 11: Credential Provider to Shopping Agent: Payment token. This step crosses a trust boundary. Step 12: Shopping Agent to Merchant: Token plus closed Checkout Mandate. This step crosses a trust boundary. If The hash of the merchant's checkout_jwt does not equal checkout_hash: The merchant returns a Checkout Receipt JWT with status Error. If A verification step fails for any other reason: The merchant must return a Checkout Receipt JWT carrying the error. Step 13: Merchant to Merchant Payment Processor: Initiate payment with the token and the checkout_jwt hash. This step crosses a trust boundary. Step 14: Merchant Payment Processor to Merchant Payment Processor: Verify the Payment Mandate inside the token. If transaction_id does not match the checkout_jwt hash: The payment is refused and a Payment Receipt with status Error goes back. Step 15: Merchant Payment Processor to Shopping Agent: Payment Receipt (also to the Credential Provider and Network). This step crosses a trust boundary. Step 16: Merchant to Shopping Agent: Checkout Receipt. This step crosses a trust boundary.

diagrams.title: AP2 v0.2 mandate lifecycle (open and closed mandates, presentation and receipts)
diagrams.description: State diagram: AP2 v0.2 mandate lifecycle (open and closed mandates, presentation and receipts). 10 states: Mandate Content drafted, Open mandate signed, Closed mandate signed, Presented to a verifier, Accepted (receipt status Success), Rejected, fallback possible, Rejected, terminal, Open mandate narrowed or used up, Purchase evidence stored, and Expired. Starts in Mandate Content drafted. Ends in Rejected, terminal, Purchase evidence stored, and Expired. 14 transitions. From Mandate Content drafted to Open mandate signed when User approves constraints on the Trusted Surface (Trusted Surface signs with user_sk (or OpenID4VP transaction_data type delegate)). From Mandate Content drafted to Closed mandate signed when User approves the exact checkout on the Trusted Surface (Trusted Surface signs mandate.checkout.1 and mandate.payment.1 with user_sk). From Open mandate signed to Closed mandate signed when Agent finds a checkout that fits the constraints (Agent signs a key-binding JWT with the key in cnf (sd_hash over the open mandate)). From Closed mandate signed to Presented to a verifier when Agent presents the mandate chain (Payment Mandate to the Credential Provider; Checkout Mandate with the token to the Merchant). From Presented to a verifier to Accepted (receipt status Success) when Verifier checks chain, bindings and constraints (Receipt JWT with status Success). From Presented to a verifier to Rejected, fallback possible when Constraint cannot be confirmed, unknown constraint, or mandates not used (Receipt JWT with status Error, error unresolved_constraint or mandates_not_supported). From Presented to a verifier to Rejected, terminal when Signature or chain fails, or the mandate does not approve the action (Receipt JWT with status Error, error invalid_credential or invalid_mandate). From Rejected, fallback possible to Mandate Content drafted when Fallback: user brought back to approve a closed mandate (New request to the Trusted Surface). From Rejected, fallback possible to Open mandate signed when Agent may try a different closed mandate from the same open mandate (Error receipt held by the agent). From Accepted (receipt status Success) to Open mandate narrowed or used up when Success receipt for an agent-signed mandate (Agent stores open, closed and receipt tuple). From Accepted (receipt status Success) to Purchase evidence stored when Both receipts returned (Payment Receipt from the processor, Checkout Receipt from the Merchant). From Open mandate narrowed or used up to Closed mandate signed when Budget or recurrence still allows another purchase (payment.budget and payment.agent_recurrence evaluated against earlier presentations). From Open mandate signed to Expired when exp reached before use (exp (Unix epoch) on the mandate). From Open mandate narrowed or used up to Expired when exp reached (exp (Unix epoch) on the mandate).
lines: From Mandate Content drafted to Open mandate signed when User approves constraints on the Trusted Surface (Trusted Surface signs with user_sk (or OpenID4VP transaction_data type delegate)).
From Mandate Content drafted to Closed mandate signed when User approves the exact checkout on the Trusted Surface (Trusted Surface signs mandate.checkout.1 and mandate.payment.1 with user_sk).
From Open mandate signed to Closed mandate signed when Agent finds a checkout that fits the constraints (Agent signs a key-binding JWT with the key in cnf (sd_hash over the open mandate)).
From Closed mandate signed to Presented to a verifier when Agent presents the mandate chain (Payment Mandate to the Credential Provider; Checkout Mandate with the token to the Merchant).
From Presented to a verifier to Accepted (receipt status Success) when Verifier checks chain, bindings and constraints (Receipt JWT with status Success).

From Presented to a verifier to Rejected, fallback possible when Constraint cannot be confirmed, unknown constraint, or mandates not used (Receipt JWT with status Error, error unresolved_constraint or mandates_not_supported).

From Presented to a verifier to Rejected, terminal when Signature or chain fails, or the mandate does not approve the action (Receipt JWT with status Error, error invalid_credential or invalid_mandate).
From Rejected, fallback possible to Mandate Content drafted when Fallback: user brought back to approve a closed mandate (New request to the Trusted Surface).
From Rejected, fallback possible to Open mandate signed when Agent may try a different closed mandate from the same open mandate (Error receipt held by the agent).
From Accepted (receipt status Success) to Open mandate narrowed or used up when Success receipt for an agent-signed mandate (Agent stores open, closed and receipt tuple).
From Accepted (receipt status Success) to Purchase evidence stored when Both receipts returned (Payment Receipt from the processor, Checkout Receipt from the Merchant).

From Open mandate narrowed or used up to Closed mandate signed when Budget or recurrence still allows another purchase (payment.budget and payment.agent_recurrence evaluated against earlier presentations).
From Open mandate signed to Expired when exp reached before use (exp (Unix epoch) on the mandate).
From Open mandate narrowed or used up to Expired when exp reached (exp (Unix epoch) on the mandate).

diagrams.title: AP2 alternative path: User Credential delegation with OpenID4VP and the Digital Credentials API
diagrams.description: Sequence diagram: AP2 alternative path: User Credential delegation with OpenID4VP and the Digital Credentials API. 4 participants: Shopping Agent, Browser or OS (Digital Credentials API), Wallet (Trusted Surface), and User. 5 steps, 4 crossing a trust boundary, 1 failure branch. Based on ap2 v0.2 (2026-04-28). Step 1: Shopping Agent to Browser or OS (Digital Credentials API): OpenID4VP request with a delegate entry in transaction_data. This step crosses a trust boundary. Step 2: Browser or OS (Digital Credentials API) to Wallet (Trusted Surface): Route the request to the user's wallet. This step crosses a trust boundary. Step 3: Wallet (Trusted Surface) to User: Show the purchase; authenticate. If No credential matches the DCQL query: No response is returned; the agent cannot obtain a user-signed mandate this way. Step 4: Wallet (Trusted Surface) to Browser or OS (Digital Credentials API): Authorization response: vp_token with key binding over delegate_payload. This step crosses a trust boundary. Step 5: Browser or OS (Digital Credentials API) to Shopping Agent: Return the response to the agent. This step crosses a trust boundary.

diagrams.title: ERC-8004 failure: self-feedback and the fresh-address loophole
diagrams.description: Sequence diagram: ERC-8004 failure: self-feedback and the fresh-address loophole. 4 participants: Agent owner, Fresh address controlled by the owner, Reputation Registry, and Reader with a trusted list. 4 steps, 2 crossing a trust boundary, 1 failure branch. Based on erc-8004 Draft (text of 2026-01-25) (2026-01-25). Step 1: Agent owner to Reputation Registry: giveFeedback(4242, 100, 0, "starred", ...). This step crosses a trust boundary. This step crosses a trust boundary. Step 3: Reputation Registry to Reader with a trusted list: Return NewFeedback. Step 4: Reader with a trusted list to Reputation Registry: getSummary(4242, trustedClients, "starred", "").

diagrams.title: ERC-8004 failure: wallet binding with a bad deadline
diagrams.description: Sequence diagram: ERC-8004 failure: wallet binding with a bad deadline. 3 participants: Agent owner, New agent wallet, and Identity Registry. 5 steps, 4 crossing a trust boundary, 2 failure branches. Based on erc-8004 Draft (text of 2026-01-25) (2026-01-25). Step 1: Agent owner to New agent wallet: Request AgentWalletSet with a 30-minute deadline. This step crosses a trust boundary. Step 2: Agent owner to Identity Registry: setAgentWallet(...). This step crosses a trust boundary. If deadline is more than 5 minutes after the block time: Reverts with "deadline too far". No state changes. Step 3: Agent owner to New agent wallet: Request a new signature with a 4-minute deadline. This step crosses a trust boundary. Step 4: Agent owner to Identity Registry: Submit after 6 minutes. This step crosses a trust boundary. If block time is after the deadline: Reverts with "expired". The wallet keeps its previous value. Step 5: Agent owner to Identity Registry: Retry with a fresh signature.

diagrams.title: ERC-8004 feedback with proof of payment after an x402 payment
diagrams.description: Sequence diagram: ERC-8004 feedback with proof of payment after an x402 payment. 6 participants: Client agent, Seller agent (x402 server), x402 facilitator, IPFS or HTTPS host, Reputation Registry, and Indexer or reader. 8 steps, 5 crossing a trust boundary, 5 failure branches. Based on erc-8004 Draft (text of 2026-01-25) (2026-01-25). Step 1: Client agent to Seller agent (x402 server): Pay for a call with x402. This step crosses a trust boundary. Step 2: Seller agent (x402 server) to x402 facilitator: Verify and settle. This step crosses a trust boundary. Step 3: Seller agent (x402 server) to Client agent: Return 200 with PAYMENT-RESPONSE. Step 4: Client agent to IPFS or HTTPS host: Upload feedback file with proofOfPayment. This step crosses a trust boundary. Step 5: Client agent to Client agent: Compute feedbackHash. Step 6: Client agent to Reputation Registry: giveFeedback(agentId, value, valueDecimals, tag1, tag2, endpoint, feedbackURI, feedbackHash). This step crosses a trust boundary. If The caller is the owner or an operator of the agent: Reverts with "Self-feedback not allowed". If valueDecimals is above 18: Reverts with "too many decimals". If The agentId does not exist: Reverts with ERC721NonexistentToken. Step 7: Reputation Registry to Indexer or reader: Return NewFeedback event. Step 8: Indexer or reader to IPFS or HTTPS host: Fetch the file and check the proof. This step crosses a trust boundary. If The file is gone or its hash does not match: The on-chain value still counts in getSummary; only off-chain scoring can discount it. If The txHash does not exist or pays someone else: Nothing on-chain flags it; the reader must reject it.

diagrams.title: ERC-8004 agent identity lifecycle (Identity Registry)
diagrams.description: State diagram: ERC-8004 agent identity lifecycle (Identity Registry). 6 states: Not registered, Registered, no URI, Registered with URI, wallet = owner, Wallet verified, Wallet cleared, and Declared inactive (off-chain only). Starts in Not registered. 17 transitions. From Not registered to Registered, no URI when Mint without a URI (register()). From Not registered to Registered with URI, wallet = owner when Mint with a URI (register(agentURI) or register(agentURI, metadata)). From Registered, no URI to Registered with URI, wallet = owner when Owner or operator sets the URI (setAgentURI(agentId, newURI)). From Registered with URI, wallet = owner to Registered with URI, wallet = owner when File moved or edited (setAgentURI(agentId, newURI)). From Registered with URI, wallet = owner to Wallet verified when New wallet signs AgentWalletSet within 5 minutes (setAgentWallet(agentId, newWallet, deadline, signature)). From Wallet verified to Wallet cleared when Owner or operator clears the wallet (unsetAgentWallet(agentId)). From Registered with URI, wallet = owner to Wallet cleared when Token transferred to a new owner (ERC-721 transferFrom or safeTransferFrom). From Wallet verified to Wallet cleared when Token transferred to a new owner (ERC-721 transferFrom or safeTransferFrom). From Wallet cleared to Wallet verified when Current owner binds a wallet again (setAgentWallet(agentId, newWallet, deadline, signature)). From Registered with URI, wallet = owner to Declared inactive (off-chain only) when Owner publishes a file with active false (setAgentURI(agentId, newURI) or an HTTPS file edit). From Wallet verified to Declared inactive (off-chain only) when Owner publishes a file with active false (setAgentURI(agentId, newURI) or an HTTPS file edit). From Declared inactive (off-chain only) to Registered with URI, wallet = owner when Owner publishes a file with active true (wallet state unchanged) (setAgentURI(agentId, newURI)). diagrams.title: Agentic token lifecycle (as described, not a published state model)
diagrams.description: State diagram: Agentic token lifecycle (as described, not a published state model). 8 states: Agent registered, Agent certified, Consumer authorized, Token provisioned, Presented at checkout, Authorized, Declined, and Expired or no longer usable. Starts in Agent registered. Ends in Authorized, Declined, and Expired or no longer usable. 8 transitions. From Agent registered to Agent certified when Security review and certification pass. From Agent certified to Consumer authorized when Consumer authenticates with the platform and authorizes the agent. From Consumer authorized to Token provisioned when Platform requests an agentic token (Not published). From Token provisioned to Presented at checkout when Agent fills the card form or calls the merchant API. From Presented at checkout to Authorized when Network detokenizes and issuer approves (Card authorization message). From Presented at checkout to Declined when Outside token limits or issuer declines (Card authorization message). From Token provisioned to Expired or no longer usable when Time window passes or single use consumed. From Authorized to Expired or no longer usable when Single-use token cannot be used again.

From Agent certified to Consumer authorized when Consumer authenticates with the platform and authorizes the agent.
From Consumer authorized to Token provisioned when Platform requests an agentic token (Not published).
From Token provisioned to Presented at checkout when Agent fills the card form or calls the merchant API.
From Presented at checkout to Authorized when Network detokenizes and issuer approves (Card authorization message).
From Presented at checkout to Declined when Outside token limits or issuer declines (Card authorization message).
From Token provisioned to Expired or no longer usable when Time window passes or single use consumed.

diagrams.title: An agent buys one API call: discovery, x402 exact payment, ERC-8004 feedback
diagrams.description: Sequence diagram: An agent buys one API call: discovery, x402 exact payment, ERC-8004 feedback. 9 participants: Client agent, Bazaar discovery endpoint, ERC-8004 Identity Registry, IPFS or HTTPS host, Seller resource server, x402 facilitator, Token contract (EVM chain), ERC-8004 Reputation Registry, and Indexer or reader. 14 steps, 13 crossing a trust boundary, 13 failure branches. Based on several protocols x402 v2.0; ERC-8004 Draft (text of 2026-01-25) (2026-01-25). Step 1: Client agent to Bazaar discovery endpoint: GET /discovery/resources (Bazaar). This step crosses a trust boundary. If The listing is stale and the server now asks for more: The live 402 response wins; the client must compare it with its budget again. Step 2: Client agent to ERC-8004 Identity Registry: Read tokenURI and getAgentWallet (ERC-8004). This step crosses a trust boundary. If The agent NFT was transferred: agentWallet was cleared on transfer; getAgentWallet returns no wallet until the new owner binds one again. Step 3: Client agent to IPFS or HTTPS host: Fetch the registration file. This step crosses a trust boundary. If The file is gone or does not list the endpoint: Nothing on chain flags it; the client should not pay that endpoint. Step 4: Client agent to Seller resource server: GET /weather (no payment header). This step crosses a trust boundary. Step 5: Seller resource server to Client agent: 402 Payment Required with PAYMENT-REQUIRED. This step crosses a trust boundary. Step 6: Client agent to Client agent: Check payTo against agentWallet, sign EIP-3009. If payTo differs from the agent's agentWallet: Neither protocol forces this check; a client that skips it can pay an address the agent never verified. If The amount is above the spend cap: The SDK rejects the entry and no payment is created. Step 7: Client agent to Seller resource server: Retry with PAYMENT-SIGNATURE. This step crosses a trust boundary. If The header is malformed: The server answers 400 (invalid payment). Step 8: Seller resource server to x402 facilitator: POST /verify, run the handler. This step crosses a trust boundary. If isValid is false (for example insufficient_funds or invalid_exact_evm_payload_signature): The server answers 402 again and the handler does not run. If The handler fails: The server does not settle, so the client is not charged. Step 9: Seller resource server to x402 facilitator: POST /settle. This step crosses a trust boundary. If The settle call times out or returns settlement_pending: The outcome is indeterminate; the server must reconcile the broadcast hash before it retries. Step 10: x402 facilitator to Token contract (EVM chain): transferWithAuthorization (facilitator pays gas). This step crosses a trust boundary. If The nonce was used or the balance dropped: The transaction reverts and the facilitator returns success false. Step 11: Seller resource server to Client agent: 200 OK with PAYMENT-RESPONSE. This step crosses a trust boundary. Step 12: Client agent to IPFS or HTTPS host: Publish the feedback file with proofOfPayment. This step crosses a trust boundary. Step 13: Client agent to ERC-8004 Reputation Registry: giveFeedback(agentId, value, valueDecimals, tag1, tag2, endpoint, feedbackURI, feedbackHash). This step crosses a trust boundary. If The caller owns or operates the agent: Reverts with "Self-feedback not allowed". If valueDecimals is above 18: Reverts with "too many decimals". Step 14: Indexer or reader to IPFS or HTTPS host: Fetch the file, check hash and txHash. This step crosses a trust boundary. If The txHash does not exist or pays someone else: Nothing on chain flags it and getSummary still counts the value; only off-chain scoring can discount it.

diagrams.description: Sequence diagram: An agent shops on a merchant website with a Visa card: TAP browsing and payer signatures, a VIC token, verification at the CDN. 7 participants: Consumer, AI agent (Agent Provider), Visa Intelligent Commerce, CDN (Site Protection Provider), Visa key store, Merchant website, and Acquirer, Visa network and issuer. 16 steps, 13 crossing a trust boundary, 11 failure branches. Based on several protocols TAP spec, unversioned (read 2026-10-11); VIC API client in visa/ai (2026-09-30) (2025-10-14). Step 1: Consumer to AI agent (Agent Provider): Ask the agent to buy an item. Step 2: AI agent (Agent Provider) to Visa Intelligent Commerce: POST /vacp/v1/cards (card enrollment). This step crosses a trust boundary. If Step-up verification fails: No agent-specific token is provisioned. Step 3: AI agent (Agent Provider) to CDN (Site Protection Provider): GET product page, signed with tag agent-browser-auth. This step crosses a trust boundary. If A checkout enabler or proxy strips the signature headers: The request arrives untagged and is treated as an unknown bot. Step 4: CDN (Site Protection Provider) to Visa key store: Fetch the key for keyid. This step crosses a trust boundary. If No key for keyid, or the key has expired: Block the request; TAP has no revocation list or key status endpoint. Step 5: CDN (Site Protection Provider) to CDN (Site Protection Provider): Verify tag, fields, window, nonce and signature. If Neither agent-browser-auth nor agent-payer-auth in Signature-Input: Not signed by a trusted agent; block or apply ordinary bot policy. If Missing field, window over 8 minutes, reused nonce or failed signature: Block the request. Step 6: CDN (Site Protection Provider) to Merchant website: Forward as a verified browsing agent. This step crosses a trust boundary. Step 7: Merchant website to AI agent (Agent Provider): 200 product page with final cost. This step crosses a trust boundary. Step 8: AI agent (Agent Provider) to Visa Intelligent Commerce: POST /vacp/v1/instructions (Payment Instruction). This step crosses a trust boundary. Step 9: Consumer to Visa Intelligent Commerce: Approve the instruction with a passkey. This step crosses a trust boundary. If The consumer declines or the passkey check fails: No credentials can be retrieved; nothing is charged. Step 10: AI agent (Agent Provider) to Visa Intelligent Commerce: POST /vacp/v1/instructions/{instructionId}/credentials. This step crosses a trust boundary. Step 11: AI agent (Agent Provider) to CDN (Site Protection Provider): POST checkout, signed with tag agent-payer-auth, with agenticConsumer and agenticPaymentContainer. This step crosses a trust boundary. If The body is altered in transit: The header signature still verifies; only the body object signatures can catch it. Step 12: CDN (Site Protection Provider) to Merchant website: Verify the payer signature at the edge, forward. This step crosses a trust boundary. If The signature window has passed while the agent was waiting for the passkey: Block; the agent signs a fresh request. Step 13: Merchant website to Merchant website: Verify the body objects and the credential hash. If Payment container fields missing, nonce mismatch or bad signature: Should not be used for payment. If The merchant's hash of the key-entered card data differs from the payment credential hash: The specification says the merchant should decline. Step 14: Merchant website to Acquirer, Visa network and issuer: Authorize the card payment. This step crosses a trust boundary. If The issuer declines: An ordinary card decline; TAP has no role. Step 15: Merchant website to AI agent (Agent Provider): Order confirmation. This step crosses a trust boundary. Step 16: AI agent (Agent Provider) to Visa Intelligent Commerce: POST /vacp/v1/instructions/{instructionId}/confirmations. This step crosses a trust boundary.

If Key not found in the directory: Mastercard's Level 1 decision table blocks the request. Step 4: CDN or merchant edge to Merchant checkout: Verify window, nonce, tag and signature, then forward. This step crosses a trust boundary. If No Signature-Input or no scheme tag: Sent to the merchant's non-agent bot policy. If A required field is missing: Blocked. Step 5: Merchant checkout to Agent platform (registered agent): Checkout page with standard card fields (and a checkout_jwt, per spec). This step crosses a trust boundary. Step 8: Agent platform (registered agent) to Agent platform (registered agent): Sign L3a and L3b linked by checkout_hash (specified; live use not shown publicly). Step 10: Agent platform (registered agent) to Merchant checkout: Present L1, L2 and L3b to the merchant (specified; transport not defined). This step crosses a trust boundary. diagrams.title: Metered inference: an MPP session on Tempo with vouchers, a top-up and a cooperative close
diagrams.description: Sequence diagram: Metered inference: an MPP session on Tempo with vouchers, a top-up and a cooperative close. 3 participants: Client agent, Inference API server, and Tempo channel escrow (TIP-20 precompile in v2). 13 steps, 10 crossing a trust boundary, 9 failure branches. Based on several protocols MPP core draft-httpauth-payment-01; Tempo session draft-tempo-session-00 (v2 text merged 2026-06-25) (2026-06-25). Step 1: Client agent to Inference API server: POST /v1/chat/completions with Accept-Payment. This step crosses a trust boundary. Step 2: Inference API server to Client agent: 402 with WWW-Authenticate: Payment, method tempo, intent session. This step crosses a trust boundary. Step 3: Client agent to Client agent: Choose a deposit, sign the open transaction and a zero voucher. Step 4: Client agent to Inference API server: Retry with Authorization: Payment, action open. This step crosses a trust boundary. If The challenge id is unknown, used or expired: 402 with a fresh challenge and a matching problem type such as invalid-challenge or payment-expired. Step 5: Inference API server to Tempo channel escrow (TIP-20 precompile in v2): Broadcast the open transaction. This step crosses a trust boundary. Step 6: Inference API server to Client agent: 200, stream starts, Payment-Receipt in headers. This step crosses a trust boundary. Step 7: Client agent to Inference API server: Voucher per unit batch (action voucher, HEAD allowed). This step crosses a trust boundary. If The voucher total exceeds the deposit: Rejected (session/amount-exceeds-deposit). If The increase is below minVoucherDelta: Rejected (session/delta-too-small). If The voucher is signed by the wrong key: Rejected (session/signer-mismatch). Step 8: Inference API server to Client agent: SSE event payment-need-voucher. If No voucher arrives within the server's timeout (for example 60 seconds): The server should close the stream; the agent has paid only for what its vouchers covered. Step 9: Client agent to Inference API server: Top up (action topUp). This step crosses a trust boundary. If The challenge id is unknown or expired: Rejected with problem type challenge-not-found. Step 10: Inference API server to Tempo channel escrow (TIP-20 precompile in v2): Broadcast topUp; settle when the server chooses. This step crosses a trust boundary. Step 11: Client agent to Inference API server: Close (action close) with the final voucher. This step crosses a trust boundary. Step 12: Inference API server to Tempo channel escrow (TIP-20 precompile in v2): close: capture max(spent, settled), refund the rest. This step crosses a trust boundary. If The server never closes (forced close): The agent calls requestClose on chain; a grace period of at least 15 minutes starts in which the server can still settle or close; the spec advises waiting at least 16 minutes before withdraw, which returns all unsettled funds. If The agent tops up while a close request is pending: The topUp cancels the close request and emits CloseRequestCancelled. If A close voucher equal to the settled amount (mppx before 0.4.11, CVE-2026-34209): The vulnerable server accepted it, letting anyone close or grief a channel for free; fixed in 0.4.11. Step 13: Inference API server to Client agent: Final receipt with txHash (SSE payment-receipt event).

diagrams.title: A shopper buys running shoes in Gemini: UCP checkout, an AP2 checkout mandate (per spec), Google Pay, signed order webhooks
diagrams.description: Sequence diagram: A shopper buys running shoes in Gemini: UCP checkout, an AP2 checkout mandate (per spec), Google Pay, signed order webhooks. 7 participants: Shopper, Gemini (UCP platform, shopping agent), Trusted checkout UI (Trusted Surface), Google Pay (credential provider), Merchant (business, merchant of record), Merchant PSP (Merchant Payment Processor), and Card network and issuer. 14 steps, 10 crossing a trust boundary, 9 failure branches. Based on several protocols UCP v2026-08-25; AP2 v0.2 (2026-08-25). Step 1: Shopper to Gemini (UCP platform, shopping agent): Ask for running shoes. Step 2: Gemini (UCP platform, shopping agent) to Merchant (business, merchant of record): GET /.well-known/ucp (business profile). This step crosses a trust boundary. If The two profiles share no compatible capability: capabilities_incompatible (returned with HTTP 200 inside a UCP response). Step 3: Gemini (UCP platform, shopping agent) to Merchant (business, merchant of record): POST /checkout-sessions with UCP-Agent. This step crosses a trust boundary. Step 4: Merchant (business, merchant of record) to Gemini (UCP platform, shopping agent): Checkout with ap2.merchant_authorization. This step crosses a trust boundary. If The signature is missing or does not verify against the merchant's keys: merchant_authorization_missing or merchant_authorization_invalid; the platform must not show the checkout. If The merchant needs buyer input it cannot get through the API: status requires_escalation with continue_url; the shopper finishes on the merchant's site. Step 5: Gemini (UCP platform, shopping agent) to Trusted checkout UI (Trusted Surface): Verify the merchant signature, hand off to the trusted UI. This step crosses a trust boundary. Step 6: Shopper to Trusted checkout UI (Trusted Surface): Review and approve; choose Google Pay. Step 7: Trusted checkout UI (Trusted Surface) to Google Pay (credential provider): Run the com.google.pay handler (PAN_ONLY). This step crosses a trust boundary. If The merchant's PSP cannot process Google's tokens: The merchant cannot accept this handler; Google's FAQ makes PSP support a precondition. Step 8: Trusted checkout UI (Trusted Surface) to Trusted checkout UI (Trusted Surface): Create the closed mandates (per spec; live use unverified). Step 9: Gemini (UCP platform, shopping agent) to Merchant (business, merchant of record): POST /checkout-sessions/{id}/complete (signed, with ap2.checkout_mandate). This step crosses a trust boundary. If AP2 was negotiated but ap2.checkout_mandate is missing: mandate_required; the merchant must reject the complete. If The response to complete is lost: Retry with the same Idempotency-Key; during complete_in_progress the platform must not start a new update or complete. Step 10: Merchant (business, merchant of record) to Merchant (business, merchant of record): Verify the checkout mandate against the current checkout. If The mandate is for another checkout, expired or badly signed: mandate_scope_mismatch, mandate_expired or mandate_invalid_signature. Step 11: Merchant (business, merchant of record) to Merchant PSP (Merchant Payment Processor): Authorize the Google Pay token; processor checks the payment mandate. This step crosses a trust boundary. Step 12: Merchant PSP (Merchant Payment Processor) to Card network and issuer: Card authorization. This step crosses a trust boundary. If The issuer declines: The merchant returns a payment failure in the checkout; no order is created. Step 13: Merchant (business, merchant of record) to Gemini (UCP platform, shopping agent): completed with order; receipts. This step crosses a trust boundary. Step 14: Merchant (business, merchant of record) to Gemini (UCP platform, shopping agent): Order webhook, RFC 9421 signed. This step crosses a trust boundary. If The webhook signer is not the order's business: The platform must reject the event.

diagrams.title: Tempo session channel lifecycle (cooperative and forced close)
diagrams.description: State diagram: Tempo session channel lifecycle (cooperative and forced close). 6 states: Session challenge issued, Channel open, Streaming with vouchers, Close requested (grace period), Closed and finalized, and Rejected. Starts in Session challenge issued. Ends in Closed and finalized and Rejected. 11 transitions. From Session challenge issued to Channel open when Client sends action open with a signed deposit transaction (open(payee, token, deposit, salt, authorizedSigner)). From Session challenge issued to Rejected when Open transaction or voucher signature invalid (HTTP 402 session/invalid-signature). From Channel open to Streaming with vouchers when Client sends rising vouchers to the same URI (Authorization: Payment action voucher (HEAD allowed)). From Streaming with vouchers to Streaming with vouchers when Server claims the newest voucher (settle(channelId, cumulativeAmount, signature)). From Streaming with vouchers to Streaming with vouchers when Deposit runs low (action topUp; topUp(channelId, additionalDeposit)). From Streaming with vouchers to Closed and finalized when Cooperative close: client sends action close; server captures max(spent, settled) (close(channelId, cumulativeAmount, signature)). From Streaming with vouchers to Close requested (grace period) when Server stops answering; client starts a forced close (requestClose(channelId)). From Close requested (grace period) to Streaming with vouchers when Client tops up, which cancels the close request (topUp (emits CloseRequestCancelled)). From Close requested (grace period) to Closed and finalized when Server closes during the grace period (close(channelId, cumulativeAmount, signature)). From Close requested (grace period) to Closed and finalized when Grace period over (wait 16 minutes); client withdraws the rest (withdraw(channelId)). From Streaming with vouchers to Rejected when Voucher above deposit, below minVoucherDelta or from the wrong signer (HTTP 402 session/amount-exceeds-deposit, session/delta-too-small, session/signer-mismatch).

diagrams.description: Sequence diagram: Visa TAP: browse a product, then check out with signed objects. 5 participants: AI agent, Site Protection Provider (CDN), Visa key store, Merchant, and Acquirer and Visa network. 11 steps, 8 crossing a trust boundary, 8 failure branches. Based on visa-tap TAP spec, unversioned (read 2026-10-11) (2025-10-14). Step 1: AI agent to Site Protection Provider (CDN): GET product page, signed agent-browser-auth. diagrams.title: x402 payment lifecycle (V2, all three payment flows)
diagrams.description: State diagram: x402 payment lifecycle (V2, all three payment flows). 11 states: Unpaid request, Payment required (402), Payload received, Verified, Committed before execution, Handler executed, Settlement pending, Settled, Rejected, Responded 200, and Voided or reclaimed. Starts in Unpaid request. Ends in Rejected, Responded 200, and Voided or reclaimed. 18 transitions. From Unpaid request to Payment required (402) when Server sends 402 (HTTP 402 + PAYMENT-REQUIRED). From Payment required (402) to Payload received when Client retries with a signed payload (PAYMENT-SIGNATURE header). From Payload received to Rejected when Malformed payload or unsupported scheme, network or flow (HTTP 400). From Payload received to Verified when authorization flow: facilitator returns isValid true (POST /verify). From Payload received to Rejected when Facilitator returns isValid false (POST /verify, then HTTP 402). From Payload received to Rejected when Facilitator unreachable (@x402/express answers 502; SDK behavior, not in the spec) (HTTP 502). From Payload received to Committed before execution when upfront or escrow flow: first settle succeeds (POST /settle). From Verified to Handler executed when Handler runs. From Committed before execution to Handler executed when Handler runs. From Handler executed to Settled when authorization flow: settle succeeds, or escrow: capture succeeds (POST /settle). From Handler executed to Settlement pending when Settle broadcast but not confirmed, or timed out (POST /settle). From Settlement pending to Settled when Server reconciles on chain and finds the transfer. From Settlement pending to Rejected when Reconciliation shows no transfer and one retry fails (POST /settle). From Handler executed to Rejected when Settle fails (for example insufficient_funds) (HTTP 402 + PAYMENT-RESPONSE success false). From Handler executed to Voided or reclaimed when escrow: server voids the hold (POST /settle with payload.type void). Based on x402 v2.0 (2025-12-09). Step 1: Client (agent) to Resource server: GET /article/A. Step 2: Resource server to Client (agent): 402 with a fresh BOLT11 invoice. Step 3: Client (agent) to Lightning Network: Pay the invoice. This step crosses a trust boundary. If The invoice expired (maxTimeoutSeconds equals the invoice expiry): The payment fails; the client requests a new 402. Step 4: Client (agent) to Resource server: Retry with PAYMENT-SIGNATURE (preimage). Step 5: Resource server to Facilitator: POST /settle (no /verify). This step crosses a trust boundary. If The preimage does not match, or the payment hash was already recorded: Settle fails and the handler does not run. A replay is refused. Step 6: Facilitator to Resource server: Return SettleResponse success true. Step 7: Resource server to Resource server: Run the handler. If The handler fails after settlement: The client paid for nothing; any remedy is the server's own arrangement. Step 8: Resource server to Client (agent): 200 OK with PAYMENT-RESPONSE.

diagrams.title: x402 V2 over HTTP: exact scheme, authorization payment flow
diagrams.description: Sequence diagram: x402 V2 over HTTP: exact scheme, authorization payment flow. 4 participants: Client (agent), Resource server, Facilitator, and Base Sepolia. 13 steps, 4 crossing a trust boundary, 10 failure branches. Based on x402 v2.0 (2025-12-09). Step 1: Client (agent) to Resource server: GET /weather (no payment header). Step 2: Resource server to Client (agent): 402 Payment Required with PAYMENT-REQUIRED. If A route has no registered scheme: Since @x402/core 2.25.0 the SDK throws an error instead of answering 402 with an empty accepts list. Step 3: Client (agent) to Client (agent): Choose an accepts entry, check limits, sign EIP-712. If Amount is above the spend cap or the asset is not allowed: The SDK rejects the entry; if no entry is left, no payment is created. If The entry names a paymentFlow the client does not recognize: The client must skip that entry. Step 4: Client (agent) to Resource server: Retry GET /weather with PAYMENT-SIGNATURE. If The header is malformed: The server answers 400 (invalid payment). Step 5: Resource server to Facilitator: POST /verify. This step crosses a trust boundary. If The facilitator is unreachable or times out: See the facilitator-down flow: the Express middleware answers 502 and the handler does not run. Step 6: Facilitator to Base Sepolia: Read balance and nonce state, simulate. This step crosses a trust boundary. Step 7: Facilitator to Resource server: Return VerifyResponse isValid true. If isValid is false (for example expired window, wrong recipient, used nonce, low balance): The server answers 402 and the handler does not run. See the failure flows. Step 8: Resource server to Resource server: Run the handler. If The handler fails: The server does not settle, so the client is not charged (an SDK hook, settleOnCancel, can change this). Step 9: Resource server to Facilitator: POST /settle. This step crosses a trust boundary. If The settle call times out: The outcome is indeterminate: the transfer may still confirm, so the server must reconcile before it retries. Step 10: Facilitator to Base Sepolia: Broadcast transferWithAuthorization. This step crosses a trust boundary. If The nonce was consumed in the meantime or the balance dropped: The transaction reverts; the facilitator returns success false. Step 11: Base Sepolia to Facilitator: Return transaction receipt. Step 12: Facilitator to Resource server: Return SettleResponse success true. If errorReason is settlement_pending: Non-terminal: the transaction was broadcast but not confirmed. The response carries the hash, and the server reconciles before it decides. Step 13: Resource server to Client (agent): 200 OK with PAYMENT-RESPONSE.
lines: Step 1: Client (agent) to Resource server: GET /weather (no payment header).

Step 2: Resource server to Client (agent): 402 Payment Required with PAYMENT-REQUIRED. If A route has no registered scheme: Since @x402/core 2.25.0 the SDK throws an error instead of answering 402 with an empty accepts list.

Step 3: Client (agent) to Client (agent): Choose an accepts entry, check limits, sign EIP-712. If Amount is above the spend cap or the asset is not allowed: The SDK rejects the entry; if no entry is left, no payment is created. If The entry names a paymentFlow the client does not recognize: The client must skip that entry.
Step 4: Client (agent) to Resource server: Retry GET /weather with PAYMENT-SIGNATURE. If The header is malformed: The server answers 400 (invalid payment).

Step 5: Resource server to Facilitator: POST /verify. This step crosses a trust boundary. If The facilitator is unreachable or times out: See the facilitator-down flow: the Express middleware answers 502 and the handler does not run.
Step 6: Facilitator to Base Sepolia: Read balance and nonce state, simulate. This step crosses a trust boundary.

Step 7: Facilitator to Resource server: Return VerifyResponse isValid true. If isValid is false (for example expired window, wrong recipient, used nonce, low balance): The server answers 402 and the handler does not run. See the failure flows.
Step 8: Resource server to Resource server: Run the handler. If The handler fails: The server does not settle, so the client is not charged (an SDK hook, settleOnCancel, can change this).

Step 9: Resource server to Facilitator: POST /settle. This step crosses a trust boundary. If The settle call times out: The outcome is indeterminate: the transfer may still confirm, so the server must reconcile before it retries.

Step 10: Facilitator to Base Sepolia: Broadcast transferWithAuthorization. This step crosses a trust boundary. If The nonce was consumed in the meantime or the balance dropped: The transaction reverts; the facilitator returns success false.
Step 11: Base Sepolia to Facilitator: Return transaction receipt.

Step 12: Facilitator to Resource server: Return SettleResponse success true. If errorReason is settlement_pending: Non-terminal: the transaction was broadcast but not confirmed. The response carries the hash, and the server reconciles before it decides.
Step 13: Resource server to Client (agent): 200 OK with PAYMENT-RESPONSE.
